claims.text: The starting EHEA has dual-phase lamellar colonies and contains no nanoscale precipitates.
Controlled aging heat treatment can introduce nanoscale precipitates into the matrix phase of an EHEA.
Optimized aging can produce a uniform nanoscale-precipitate distribution without coarsening or destabilizing the lamellar structure.
The intervention will yield nanoscale precipitates uniformly distributed within the matrix phase.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the precipitates increases strength through the Orowan mechanism.
Precipitate-induced strain hardening delays microcrack initiation at internal boundaries.
The precipitates impede or delay microcrack propagation at internal boundaries.
The aged EHEA will have higher yield strength than the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The aged EHEA will have higher ultimate tensile strength than the unmodified baseline.
The aged EHEA will have significantly greater room-temperature tensile ductility than the unmodified baseline.
The unmodified dual-phase lamellar EHEA has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and is brittle.
The proposed benefit is limited to EHEAs with a stable lamellar structure and a matrix capable of hosting nanoscale precipitates.
Excessive precipitate coarsening may negate the proposed strength and ductility benefits.
Heat-treatment-induced destabilization of the lamellar structure may negate the proposed benefits.

contradictions.description: Coarsening or lamellar destabilization is presented as an excluded boundary condition that may negate the effect, but it is also treated as directly falsifying the hypothesis. A failed intervention that falls outside the stated boundary does not decisively test the hypothesis within its claimed domain.
